ingredients.item: Korean radish or daikon, peeled, cut into matchsticks 5 cm long and 5 mm thick
ingredients.preparation: a mandoline earns its drawer here

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: The dressing whisked in the big bowl while the radish weeps — gochugaru, fish sauce, honey, garlic, ginger, vinegar worked to a loose paste.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: taste on a radish off-cut: savory-sweet with a warm edge and a clean acid finish, a shade stronger than target.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: The squeezed radish and scallions tossed through the dressing, sesame last, and a 10-minute rest before serving — the rest is when the gochugaru's color blooms into the sticks.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the eating test: snap, the radish's pepper-sweet, the dressing's warm-sweet-acid in one bite — and beside a piece of grilled mackerel (#SF07) the fish tastes lighter for it. That is musaengchae's entire job, performed.

visualDonenessCues: taste on a radish off-cut: savory-sweet with a warm edge and a clean acid finish, a shade stronger than target.

the eating test: snap, the radish's pepper-sweet, the dressing's warm-sweet-acid in one bite — and beside a piece of grilled mackerel (#SF07) the fish tastes lighter for it. That is musaengchae's entire job, performed.
storageNotes: Best the day it's made; acceptable into day two refrigerated, crisper than most fresh banchan.
Variations: matchstick Asian pear folded in (the fish-table classic); the same dressing on cabbage runs geotjeori (#B04) logic; the fermented road is #B02.
